Wow!  Is this theme clever or what?  And dense.  To find four (4!!!!) in the language phrases in which each half works with HAND separately and the two halves also work with each other is inspired.  And to find the perfect revealer!  I don't think that would be something that a computer program or AI could come up with -- though of course I could be wrong.  Hope I'm not.

There's some glue, of course, when you have a theme this dense.  I will never remember what SMS is, never, and OXO, LUV, ORC and NAVI don't exactly make my heart pound.  Also, I'm perplexed by the choice for the ODE.  I know you're an important poet, Pablo, but if you're writing an ODE to your SOCKS, for heaven's sake, all I know is that it better be pretty darned special.  Socks by their very nature are seldom special.  Personally, I prefer skylarks, nightingales, Grecian Urns and Joy.

But a clever, clever theme.  The kind of theme that, when the constructor comes up with his fourth theme answer and, glory be, the symmetry works, I can imagine him leaping to his feet and shouting "Eureka!" at the top of his lungs.

I'm 50 and a bisexual guy, so I was a little surprised to SEE ONTHEDL clued in a non-sexual context. In the US, it's long-standing slang in the Black queer community for straight-presenting men who may have female partners, and who secretly also have sex with men. Like many queer terms, I think it has filtered into the straight world and is used in other contexts, but this meaning is still the main result that comes up when you Google the term, and it's the primary Wikipedia article. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Down-low_(sexual_slang)

So I just had a fascinating interaction with ChatGPT which demonstrates why it isn’t going to be solving, much less constructing, decent crossword puzzles any time soon. SPOILERS if you haven’t solved the last Crosshare puzzle I posted, “Clue Finder”:
.
.
.
I asked it to solve this puzzle, which most of you made short work of. It took about a half hour at first and didn’t get very far. It figured out the theme had to do with Columbo. It solved a lot of obvious clues and trivia but had a lot of trouble with misdirection—it could not let go of SATAN for “Rosemary’s baby?”Instead of SPRIG, for example, even though it didn’t work.

Then I asked it if it wanted a hint, which it eagerly accepted. I reminded it there could be rebuses (which it should have already known).

At that point it figured out ONE (MORE) THING and then tried to fit MORE into all the rebus spots.

After a few minutes I asked it if it wanted another hint, and told it perhaps the rebuses weren’t all the same.

It dutifully tried to work more on it with this information, then asked for another hint about what was connecting all the rebuses. I told it that the revealer should be all the hint it needed.

It still was not able to complete the puzzle and I told it to give up.

So for all the pernicious abilities of this AI it still couldn’t solve a pretty simple rebus puzzle. I can sleep a little easier tonight.

@Vaer 

Quick: an tenth to a hundredth of an erg is thunit you’d use to measure the kinetic energy of an ant going about its business. 


Elaborated:

an erg is the CGS (centimetre, gram, second system of units) equivalent of the joule (MKS metre, kilogram, second which became Systeme International) and it takes 10 million ergs to make a joule. A watt is a joule per second. You know a watt because your iron at home uses about a 1000 watts when you are ironing the shirts. (I was going to use a kettle as an example but I recalled that electric kettles are rare in the US due to your low voltage system).  So you can see that in daily use you’d have a hard time using ergs.
@Andrzej Erg is the main unit of energy in the non-metric system. The analogous unit in the metric (SI) system is the joule.

The best socks to wear with sneakers are short tennis or running socks because they don't bunch up and cause blisters on long walks.  But how to keep your legs warm when the weather turns cold?  Tights with feet attached bunch up.  Knee socks bunch up.

Answer:  Once a pair of my knee socks sprouts holes in the toes or the heel, I cut off the feet and save the leg portion.  I tuck them into my tennis socks and use the combo as leg warmers in the winter.
